title: Linux File Permission Denied and POSIX ACL Mask Issue
symptom: User or service receives 'Permission denied' trying to read or execute a file despite group membership.
initial_observations: ls -la displays permissions ending in '+' symbol.
Standard chmod does not grant expected access.
environment: Linux server using POSIX Access Control Lists (ACLs).

possible_causes.cause: POSIX ACL mask restricts effective permissions or parent directory lacks execute (x) traversal bit
possible_causes.evidence_needed: getfacl shows `mask::r--` or parent directory is `drw-r--r--`.
possible_causes.remediation: Fix parent directory traversal bit (`chmod +x parent_dir`) and adjust ACL mask (`setfacl -m m::rwx file`).

investigation_steps.title: Inspect File and Parent Directory POSIX ACLs
investigation_steps.explanation: Retrieve extended ACL permissions and effective mask.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Look for #effective: annotations and mask line.

investigation_steps.title: Check Parent Directory Traversal (Execute) Permission
investigation_steps.explanation: Step through every directory in the path to verify traversal permissions.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Any parent directory missing execute (x) bit for the executing user.

prevention: Standardize file ownership and use POSIX groups rather than ad-hoc user ACLs where possible.
